source.title: Towards Understanding the Transferability of Deep Representations
source.authors: Hong Liu; Mingsheng Long; Jian-Min Wang; Michael I. Jordan

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including appendices; no truncation or garbling material to this extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own transfer-learning experiments on target-task training and test errors, weight changes, and loss landscapes in pretrained and randomly initialized networks. These results concern generalization gaps and measured properties, but do not test the claim's random-label memorization premise or most listed recipe comparisons.
record.gate_note: Rows cover target-task training/test error comparisons, pretrained-weight deviation, Hessian eigenvalues, and landscape variation. Figure-only comparisons are recorded without reconstructed values. The paper's cited findings from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests transfer learning, which none of V1–V8 names. Its Hessian eigenvalues, filter-normalized landscape visualizations, and gradient-direction loss variation do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its association with generalization gaps. Related flatness findings do not constitute a partial test of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that pretraining improves target generalization and optimization when source and target tasks are sufficiently similar in both inputs and labels. They interpret transfer initialization as implicit regularization that keeps parameters near a pretrained flat region, and also report that transferability can decline with continued pretraining.
record.recipe_differences: Studies transfer initialization and fine-tuning, comparing ImageNet-pretrained weights with random initialization; it does not use the original claim's random-label, width-sweep, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or example-removal recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer outcomes vary with source-target input and label similarity, target dataset, and pretraining epoch; transferability first rises and then declines during pretraining. These are not recipe conditions in V1–V8.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretrained networks have smaller leading Hessian eigenvalues at convergence, smoother initialization landscapes, and smaller gradient-direction loss variation than randomly initialized networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining can improve loss-landscape geometry and optimization stability relative to random initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Target errors differ across transfer datasets despite nearly zero training errors; smaller normalized deviations from pretrained weights are associated with better generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preservation of pretrained parameters is associated with target-task generalization in transfer learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5 reports that transfer benefits depend on both input and label similarity. Food-101 pretraining initially improves transfer to CUB-200, but further pretraining reduces target accuracy while source accuracy continues improving.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transfer benefits depend on source–target task similarity and pretraining duration; better source performance need not imply better transfer.

record.code_released: Codes and visualizations will be available online; no URL stated.
record.problems: Several relevant comparisons are figure-only with no reported numerical values or uncertainty. The paper does not directly measure the magnitude-aware sharpness criterion or compare it against norm- and margin-based measures. Table 1 values are reported with ± quantities, but the text does not identify those quantities in the supplied excerpt.
record.rows_left_out: None. Cited results from prior work and theoretical statements without an empirical outcome row for the listed versions were not entered as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning breadth, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Filter-normalized visualizations do not establish these comparisons.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V7 limits_scope verdict: measuring adjacent constructs leaves V7 untested. No omitted result bears directly on V1–V8, so missing is empty. Table 1 reports ± quantities without identifying their statistical meaning.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit fixed random labels or compare held-out random-label performance with natural-label performance.
Does not sweep width past interpolation on one-hidden-layer networks trained from scratch.
Does not compare convolutional networks against fully connected networks trained from scratch.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or evaluate tuning breadth.
Does not compare batch sizes or large-batch training recipes.
Does not test dropout or weight decay as interventions.

Measures Hessian eigenvalues and loss landscape variation, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; tests transfer initialization against random initialization, not a single convolutional-family sweep at similarly low training loss.
Does not identify or remove memorized examples.
